Saarland 63 places · area 1 of 5

Saarbrücken · Völklingen · Saarschleife

  1. 1 Must see within Saarland

    Völklinger Hütte (Völklingen Ironworks)

    The world's only completely preserved ironworks from the heyday of industrialisation, inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1994 — the first industrial site ever so honoured. Walk the 240 m charging platform and climb the 40 m blast-furnace viewing deck; today it doubles as a monumental venue for exhibitions and festivals.

    Look for heritage site

    Rathausstraße 75-79, 66333 Völklingen, Germany

    Recommended by , ,

  2. 2 Must see within Saarland

    Stiftskirche St. Arnual

    A completed-around-1390 Gothic three-aisled basilica ranked among the most important architectural monuments of the German southwest, holding the carved gravestones of the Counts of Nassau-Saarbrücken and crowned by a Stengel cupola of 1746. It anchors St. Arnual, the medieval 'village within the city' with its own market square.

    Look for church

    Stiftskirche St. Arnual, 66119 Saarbrücken, Germany

    Recommended by , ,

  3. 3 Must see within Saarland

    Saarlandmuseum – Moderne Galerie

    One of the leading art museums of southwest Germany, its holdings running from Impressionism and the Berlin Secession through German Expressionism, the École de Paris and Informel to the present, with a sculpture garden. The modern wing of the Saarlandmuseum, recently enlarged by a new pavilion.

    Look for museum

    Bismarckstraße 11-19, 66111 Saarbrücken, Germany

    Recommended by , ,

  4. 4 Must see within Saarland

    Homburger Schlossberghöhlen

    Europe's largest man-made red-sandstone caves, twelve storeys of vaulted halls and kilometres of galleries dug from the 11th to 17th centuries beneath the ruins of Hohenburg fortress. About 800 m across the top three walkable levels are open, glowing in bands of ochre and red.

    Look for caves

    Schlossberg-Höhen-Straße 1, 66424 Homburg, Germany

    Recommended by , ,

  5. 5 Must see within Saarland

    Saarpolygon (Bergehalde Ensdorf)

    A 30 m walkable steel landmark crowning the ~150 m mining dump above Ensdorf, opened in 2016 to commemorate the end of Saar coal mining (the last pit closed here in 2012). 132 steps climb through its two pylons to a free viewing platform that seems to change shape as you move — a symbol of the region's transformation.

    Look for landmark

    Bergehalde Ensdorf, 66802 Ensdorf, Germany

    Recommended by , ,

  6. 6 Must see within Saarland

    Römische Villa Nennig

    A luxurious Roman villa whose entrance hall keeps the largest and best-preserved mosaic floor north of the Alps — over 160 m² of some three million stones showing gladiators, beast-hunts and musicians of the amphitheatre, found by a farmer in 1852. One of the outstanding works of Roman mosaic art anywhere.

    Look for archaeological site

    Römerstraße 11, 66706 Perl-Nennig, Germany

    Recommended by , ,

  7. 7 Must see within Saarland · French

    Esplanade

    Saarbrücken's two-MICHELIN-star flagship in the Nauwieser Viertel, in an 1890 Gründerzeit former school turned boutique hotel. Chef Silio Del Fabro — Gusto's Koch des Jahres 2026 — cooks supremely fresh, farm-sourced seasonal produce; the city's benchmark fine-dining table right in its creative quarter.

    Nauwieserstraße 5, 66111 Saarbrücken, Germany

    Recommended by , ,

  8. 8 Must see within Saarland · French

    Restaurant Kunz

    A century-old family restaurant-and-butcher in the village of Bliesen that has held a MICHELIN star for over two decades under Alexander and Anke Kunz. Precise French classics sit beside the house's own charcuterie and a famous Wiener Schnitzel — the Saarland's rural fine-dining destination and a Jeunes Restaurateurs member.

    Kirchstraße 22, 66606 St. Wendel-Bliesen, Germany

    Recommended by , ,

  9. 9 Must see within Saarland · French

    GästeHaus Klaus Erfort

    Saarbrücken's temple of haute cuisine, in a Wilhelminian villa with its own park; a MICHELIN-Guide fixture (long a three-star, currently two) where Klaus Erfort serves an uncompromising, produce-driven classic French menu. The Saarland's flagship fine-dining address.

    Mainzer Straße 95, 66121 Saarbrücken, Germany

    Recommended by , ,

  10. 10 Must see within Saarland · French

    Victor's Fine Dining by Christian Bau

    Germany's benchmark table right where Germany, France and Luxembourg meet, at Victor's Residenz-Schloss Berg. Christian Bau has held three MICHELIN stars uninterrupted since 2005 for a French haute cuisine fused early and brilliantly with Japanese product; ranked among the world's top ten on La Liste.

    Schloßstraße 27-29, 66706 Perl-Nennig, Germany

    Recommended by , ,

  11. 11 Must see within Saarland

    Saarschleife & Aussichtspunkt Cloef

    Saarland's signature landscape: the river doubling back on itself in a great loop 180 m below the free Cloef viewpoint at Orscholz — the most photographed view in the state.

    Look for viewpoint

    Cloefstraße, 66693 Mettlach-Orscholz, Germany

    Recommended by ,

  12. 12 Must see within Saarland

    Ludwigskirche

    Saarbrücken's landmark and the crown of baroque master builder Friedrich Joachim Stengel's 'Ludwigsplatz' ensemble — reckoned among Germany's most important Protestant churches alongside Dresden's Frauenkirche.

    Look for church

    Ludwigsplatz, 66117 Saarbrücken, Germany

    Recommended by ,

  13. 13 Must see within Saarland

    St. Johanner Markt

    The lively heart of Saarbrücken — a pedestrian old-town square of boutiques, bistros and pubs around Stengel's 1759 baroque market fountain, with a sight-axis to the castle across the Saar.

    Look for square

    Sankt Johanner Markt, 66111 Saarbrücken, Germany

    Recommended by ,

  14. 14 Must see within Saarland

    Saarbrücker Schloss & Historisches Museum Saar

    Stengel's 18th-century baroque palace on the sandstone cliff above the Saar, its centre rebuilt in glass-and-steel by Gottfried Böhm; beneath and beside it the Historisches Museum Saar tells the region's turbulent border history.

    Look for palace

    Schlossplatz 15, 66119 Saarbrücken, Germany

    Recommended by ,

  15. 15 Must see within Saarland

    Wolfspark Werner Freund

    The 8-hectare wolf park that made Merzig the 'city of wolves', home to around 20 European grey, polar, Canadian timber and Mongolian wolves in wide open enclosures. Founded by behavioural researcher Werner Freund, who lived for decades 'as a wolf among wolves'; free to walk through, with a monthly public feeding and talk.

    Look for wildlife park

    Waldstraße 204, 66663 Merzig, Germany

    Recommended by ,

  16. 16 Must see within Saarland

    Benediktinerabtei St. Mauritius Tholey

    Reckoned the oldest monastery on German soil, with roots in the 7th century on a Roman villa site and an early-Gothic abbey church of 1230-60. Newly fitted with 30 luminous windows by Mahbuba Maqsoodi and three towering choir windows by Gerhard Richter — a pilgrimage for lovers of contemporary church art, with abbey beer, wine and honey to take home.

    Look for abbey

    Benediktinerabtei St. Mauritius, 66636 Tholey, Germany

    Recommended by ,

  17. 17 Must see within Saarland · Saarländisch

    Brauhaus zum Stiefel

    Saarbrücken's oldest inn, on the St. Johanner Markt, brewing its own beer and plating the city's most robust Saarland cooking — Gefillde, the Saarland-Teller, hearty pub classics. The definitive place to eat the region's home kitchen in the capital.

    Am Stiefel 2, 66111 Saarbrücken, Germany

    Recommended by ,

  18. 18 Must see within Saarland · Saarländisch

    Kalinski Wurstwirtschaft & Gin Bar

    A cult currywurst-and-gin bar off the St. Johanner Markt using meat from Bliesgau cattle raised nearby, with vegan sauces too. Named best currywurst in Germany by the Süddeutsche Zeitung and West Germany's most popular by Falstaff (2023) — a genuine Saarbrücken institution of the young-scene kind.

    Kaltenbachstraße 4, 66111 Saarbrücken, Germany

    Recommended by ,

  19. 19 Must see within Saarland · Saarländisch

    Restaurant Quack in der Villa Weismüller

    Creative crossover cooking in a listed Jugendstil villa with a garden terrace in Alt-Saarbrücken. A MICHELIN-Guide listing and 84 Falstaff points make it one of the city's most charming higher-end tables below the two-star bench.

    Gersweiler Straße 43a, 66117 Saarbrücken, Germany

    Recommended by ,

  20. 20 Must see within Saarland · French

    Hämmerle's Restaurant

    Sternekoch Cliff Hämmerle serves classic French cooking with creative, vegetable-forward touches from the surrounding UNESCO Bliesgau biosphere, split between the fine 'Barrique' room and the more affordable 'Landgenuss'. One MICHELIN star, 16 points in Gault&Millau and 7 pans in GUSTO; at the Chef's Table the chef plates and explains each course himself.

    Bliestalstraße 110a, 66440 Blieskastel-Webenheim, Germany

    Recommended by ,

  21. 21 Must see within Saarland · French

    Die Alte Brauerei

    A MICHELIN-starred French kitchen in a green setting in the heart of St. Ingbert, 15 minutes from Saarbrücken, led by head chef Florian Dauphin and Lorena Jil. Seasonal dishes rooted in French tradition, offered à la carte or as a menu, with six guestrooms above — one of the top addresses in the Saarpfalz.

    Kaiserstraße 101, 66386 St. Ingbert, Germany

    Recommended by ,

  22. 22 Worth the detour within Saarland

    Römermuseum Schwarzenacker

    An open-air archaeological museum on the excavated Roman vicus of Schwarzenacker, a country town of some 2,000 people that lived from about the birth of Christ until its destruction by the Alemanni in 275 AD. Reconstructed streets and houses, plus a baroque garden, bring the Roman Saar to life; combine it with the Homburg caves.

    Look for archaeological museum

    Homburger Straße 38, 66424 Homburg, Germany

    Recommended by , ,

  23. 23 Worth the detour within Saarland

    Historische Altstadt Ottweiler

    A remarkably intact small old town of Renaissance and baroque houses in the former residence of the Counts of Nassau-Saarbrücken, marked by the 15th-century Zibbelkapp tower and Stengel's pavilion and widow's palace. Best explored on one of the costumed night-watchman tours.

    Look for old town

    Schlossplatz, 66564 Ottweiler, Germany

    Recommended by , ,

  24. 24 Worth the detour within Saarland

    Nauwieser Viertel

    Saarbrücken's alternative, creative quarter — a dense grid of quirky pubs, cafés, small shops and street art just east of the old town, engaged in art and music and beloved by students and locals. The city's best evening wandering, and now home to a cluster of MICHELIN-listed kitchens as well as old-school Kneipen.

    Look for nightlife district

    Nauwieser Straße, 66111 Saarbrücken, Germany

    Recommended by ,

How we choose

Every place is recommended by named sources (review-aggregator star ratings never count as the recommender), pinned to its door from a published coordinate, and status-checked. Closed places stay, flagged, so you know they’re gone.

Must see
The places to plan a visit around — graded within each area, not across the city.
Worth the detour
Strong picks, worth going out of your way for.
Deep cut
For the curious: smaller, odder, more local.

Within each area, places are ordered by tier, then by number of named sources — never by popularity. We don’t add ratings, prices or opening hours of our own. Any quoted in a write-up are the source’s, dated.

Follow changes — an RSS feed of every closure and status check in this guide, for any feed reader.

183 sights and 104 places to eat across the cross-border Greater Region — anchored on Saarbrücken and reaching to Metz & Sarreguemines (FR), Luxembourg, and Trier & the Mosel (DE). The UNESCO trio — the Völklinger Hütte, Roman Trier, and Luxembourg’s fortifications — and a food canon all its own: the Saarland Schwenker, Luxembourg’s Judd mat Gaardebounen, Lorraine quiche & mirabelle, and Mosel Riesling, out to a deep Michelin bench.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. The Greater Region’s canon crosses three countries: the Saarland Schwenker and Dibbelabbes/Gefillde, Luxembourg’s Judd mat Gaardebounen and Gromperekichelcher, Lorraine quiche & tarte aux mirabelles, and Mosel Riesling from steep-slope Weinstuben — with a deep Michelin bench (Christian Bau 3★ on the DE/FR/LU tripoint). A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

Web-searched in-language and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to a credible source — Michelin, UNESCO, Gault&Millau, the Saarbrücker Zeitung, SR, Le Républicain Lorrain, Inspire Metz, the Luxembourg Times/Luxemburger Wort, Visit Luxembourg, the Trierischer Volksfreund, DW Travel, local university & ESN guides and vetted local creators — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open. Yelp/TripAdvisor never count toward the two-source bar.
